synthesis: scout:record-check-ins (DEV-2313) exhausted a production host's memory on 2026-08-12 (~29GB marginal footprint across a measured peak of 17 concurrent processes, ~30GB headroom) and forced a reboot; the schedule has been disabled since (routes/console.php, commit 11bc23e2) and stays disabled until the ACs are met. Root cause is a chain, not a single bug: (1) every sc_positions reader wraps kit_mapping in lower(), which disables the table's case-sensitive ORDER BY primary key (3056/32732 granules vs 13/32732 exact-case); (2) the largest org has ~255k open-order addresses; (3) the recorder pulls that whole address list OUT of ClickHouse into a PHP array, re-serializes it as an inline SQL values() literal, and pushes it BACK in 2000-row chunks, per kit, per org, every cycle (~5,500 CH queries/cycle) -- this round-trip is the actual amplifier, both for duration (63-209 min cycles) and for memory ($addresses held across the 43-kit loop, array_chunk() copying the whole array per kit, $matches[] accumulating); (4) cycles this long defeat withoutOverlapping(10) -- a lock EXPIRY, not a duration cap -- so a new process starts roughly every 10 minutes and concurrency grows unbounded (~longest_cycle/10). The intended outcome (this PR, W2+W3 of the ticket's four-workstream plan) is to make the recorder compute the match server-side in ClickHouse -- lifting the matches CTE that ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's docblock already names as the DEV-1758 extension point, adapted from scans to sc_positions -- so only ~40 match rows/cycle ever cross into PHP, plus a hard concurrency ceiling that holds independent of cycle duration. W1 (the chlocal-owned sc_positions lowercase projection that fixes root cause 1) and W4 (re-enabling the schedule + production host verification) are explicitly out of scope for this platform PR.

scope.summary: Rewrite the check-in matcher so ClickHouse computes the (kit, address, hour) match server-side and returns only matches -- never an address list -- eliminating the PHP round-trip amplifier; add a hard, runtime-independent concurrency ceiling; close the AC7 silent-failure gap in the recorder's own error handling (not in ClickhouseQuery itself); and add a peak-memory regression test at a cardinality that actually exercises the failure mode the 3-address fixtures never could. ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE (open_hotlists -> address_links -> addresses, bbox-prefiltered, geoDistance <= 160.934m) is the architecture to lift per its own docblock; ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery's separate per-org enumeration step is removed from the recorder's hot path once address resolution moves inside the single per-org/per-kit CTE.

proposed_changes.change: Replace the values()-injection design with a single CTE-based query per org (or per kit -- design risk 1, unresolved) that joins sc_positions directly against open_hotlists -> address_links -> addresses (lifted from ScoutCheckInRollupQuery), keyed by lower(kit_mapping) (equality per-kit, or IN per-org pending the EXPLAIN decision), GROUP BY (kit[_mapping], address_id, hour_bucket), argMin for matched_at/lat/lng. Returns only match rows (~40/cycle at current volume), never an address list. Keep the bbox prefilter (BBOX_PAD_DEGREES), keep BOTH prunes on public_address (id IN subquery + address_links join), extract()+toFloat64OrNull for EWKT, no FINAL on the two zod tables.
proposed_changes.reason: This IS W2 -- the amplifier (AC1) and the primary duration/memory fix (AC2, AC3).
proposed_changes.ref: app/Clickhouse/Queries/ScoutCheckInRollupQuery.php:44-47,83-151 (the CTE to lift); app/Clickhouse/Queries/ScoutCheckInMatchQuery.php:90-162 (the query this replaces)

proposed_changes.change: Drop the per-org openOrderAddressesForOrg() PHP-side fetch-and-hold entirely (no $addresses array crosses into the command); call the rewritten matcher directly per org (or per kit); replace the per-match firstOrCreate loop with one bulk ScoutCheckIn::query()->insertOrIgnore($rows) against the existing unique(kit_id, address_id, hour_bucket); add the W3 concurrency-ceiling check at command start (exit early if no slot, or dispatch per-org jobs instead of looping in-process); for the failure-sensitive calls, bypass ClickhouseQuery::query()'s Throwable-swallow (call ::handle() directly, replicating the org-address caching with an explicit Cache::remember() at the call site) so the command's EXISTING per-org/per-kit try/catch blocks actually receive a thrown exception in production -- they currently never do (AC7).
proposed_changes.reason: Removes the amplifier from the command side, adds the concurrency ceiling, fixes the dead-code failure guard.

proposed_changes.change: Likely becomes unused by the recorder (address resolution moves inline into the new matcher's CTE). No other production caller exists (verified: grep finds only the recorder + its tests). Zero memory_get_peak_usage assertions exist in the suite today (verified by grep).

proposed_changes.change: New test (AC7): with app.env=production (not the existing tests' app.env=local rethrow-branch trick) and ClickHouse unreachable, assert the recorder produces a distinguishable signal that the cycle FAILED rather than legitimately found nothing -- proving the fix actually reaches the command's error handling in the one env (production) where ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows the exception.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC1: Match computed server-side in CH; no per-org address list crosses PHP; no re-serialization to SQL.
acceptance_criteria.reason: This is the core of W2 -- lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE onto sc_positions eliminates the values()-injection round-trip entirely.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC2: Duration -- full cycle at prod cardinality < 5-min cadence, measured.
acceptance_criteria.reason: The architectural change (O(matches) output, one CH statement) is designed to hit this; however true end-to-end MEASUREMENT at prod cardinality is not achievable from this pipeline (no prod execution access, no Cloud-scale local CH) -- see questions/resource_envelope.unresolved. Implement the design; the measurement step is a genuine gap.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC3: Memory -- peak RSS O(matches), budget stated; peak x plausible concurrency fits ~30GB headroom.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Direct consequence of W2's architecture (PHP never holds the address array) plus W3's ceiling bounding the multiplier; the AC6 test operationalizes the budget claim.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC4: Concurrency -- hard ceiling independent of runtime; lookback invariant holds.
acceptance_criteria.reason: W3. Mechanism (semaphore vs per-org queued jobs) is an open design question (see questions); either way the ceiling must not depend on cycle duration the way withoutOverlapping's TTL does, and lookback_minutes (15) must stay >= whatever lock/expiry value is chosen (DEV-2348 invariant, currently 10 < 15 = zero loss window).

acceptance_criteria.item: AC5: Projection proven -- single-kit 15-min EXPLAIN granules in tens; matcher query_log p50 much less than 400ms, read_rows much less than ~500k.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Explicitly cross-repo and chlocal-owned per evidence-38238 ('This ALTER does not ship on DEV-2342'); platform is SELECT-only. Cannot be completed or proven from this repo/PR.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC6: Regression tests -- a peak-memory assertion at prod-representative address cardinality (not the current 3-address fixtures). Zero memory_get_peak_usage assertions exist today.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Verified true by grep (zero hits repo-wide). New test required; see proposed_changes.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC7: Silent-failure guard -- ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows Throwable to [] in prod, so a failed match looks identical to an empty one. The recorder must distinguish 'ran, empty' from 'failed'.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Confirmed live gap: production evidence shows 94 CH-159 errors and 0 'org address enumeration failed' warnings in one 4h window (okf/concepts/scout-check-in-recorder.md Gotchas). A prior 'watermark' mitigation for this exact problem was built and reverted specifically because it still went through the swallowing ::query() wrapper and was proven dead code by a failing test (git commit 2cd844090). Fix belongs at the recorder's call sites (bypass ::query(), not ClickhouseQuery.php itself).

acceptance_criteria.item: AC8: Host verified -- pct_usable flat across a full cycle after re-enable.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Explicitly operational and prod-only per the ticket; not achievable from a code PR.

acceptance_criteria.item: AC9: Parity -- rewritten matcher and ScoutCheckInRollupQuery agree on the same inputs (one domain rule).
acceptance_criteria.reason: New parity test (see proposed_changes) seeding identical fixtures for both queries; the two queries share address-resolution/proximity/tiebreak logic even though their LHS tables (sc_positions vs scans) differ.

questions.q: Design risk 1 (ticket-flagged, MATERIAL): should the new matcher batch per-org with lower(kit_mapping) IN (...) (fewer queries, but the optimizer may ignore the IN and lose the prune) or run per-kit with equality (more queries, clean prune)?

Design risk 2 (ticket-flagged, MATERIAL): sc_positions fixes arrive ~every 3s (far denser than the LPR scans ScoutCheckInRollupQuery was tuned against), so position_window may be much larger and the bbox less selective -- does the lifted CTE's performance profile actually transfer, or does it need its own tuning (e.g. GPS decimation before the bbox, per PG-022's precedent)?

W3 mechanism: in-process N-slot semaphore (new pattern -- no Cache::lock precedent exists anywhere in app/ today, verified by grep) vs resurrecting the reverted per-org Horizon-job dispatch (App\Jobs\Scout\RecordOrgCheckIns, git commit caab5a469 -- a working prototype, reverted only because it serialized throughput at the OLD per-org duration)? With W2 collapsing per-org duration, the job route's original objection may no longer hold.

Batching granularity for the new matcher overall (per-org vs per-kit) -- tied to design risk 1, but also affects W3's ceiling shape (a per-org job maps naturally onto per-org batching; a per-kit query does not).

How do AC2 (duration measured at prod cardinality) and AC5's EXPLAIN/query_log proof actually get executed pre-merge, given this pipeline has no production execution access and no Cloud-scale local ClickHouse? Only a read-only Cloud EXPLAIN/query_log session (as evidence-38238 prescribes for W1) seems available, and that doesn't cover the full command's wall-clock.

Should the schedule stay fully disabled until ALL of W1+W2+W3 ship (current wording implies this), or could W2+W3 alone justify a supervised re-enable even before the chlocal projection (W1) lands, accepting a smaller-but-real improvement?

tests/Feature/Console/ScoutRecordCheckInsScheduleTest.php asserts the scout:record-check-ins schedule IS registered (expression, expiry, onOneServer, etc.), but routes/console.php has had that entire Schedule::command(...) block wrapped in a /* */ comment since incident-response commit 11bc23e2 (2026-08-12 21:52:56). A commented-out PHP block cannot register an event, so this test is almost certainly failing on main right now -- confirmed by static reading, not by running tests (which this task must not do unprompted). Does this PR fix/update that test, or is it accepted as a known pre-existing failure to leave alone until W4 re-enables the schedule?

Should ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery be deleted once the recorder stops calling it (no other production caller exists, verified by grep), or kept unused as a utility for a future per-org-address consumer (e.g. DEV-2258's coverage checklist, a named future consumer of a similar enumeration per okf/concepts/check-in.md)?
What is the actual mechanism to make AC7 work, given ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows every Throwable to [] in production/testing?
questions.answer: Bypass the swallowing ::query() wrapper at the recorder's specific call sites -- call ::handle() directly (replicating the org-address caching, if any address enumeration remains, via an explicit Cache::remember() at the call site rather than ClickhouseQuery's built-in cache path) so the command's EXISTING per-org/per-kit try/catch blocks actually receive the exception in production. Do not change ClickhouseQuery.php itself (blast radius: every CH query class in the app relies on its current swallow-in-prod behavior for resilience). This is grounded in git history: a prior 'advance-on-clean-pass watermark' mitigation for this exact AC was built and then proven dead code by a failing test specifically because it still went through ::query() (commit 2cd844090, 'the advance-on-clean-pass watermark guard is dead code in production because ClickhouseQuery swallows Throwable to []').

GIT-HISTORY FIND: the per-org Horizon-job dispatch pattern for W3 already exists, once-built, in git history -- App\Jobs\Scout\RecordOrgCheckIns at commit caab5a469 (deleted at 102a3430). REPO CONVENTION: config/scout.php's own docblock states call sites read its values WITHOUT a fallback 'so a value can never disagree with itself (DEV-2342 shipped one knob with three different defaults)' -- any new W3 tunable must follow this discipline.

ARCHITECTURAL PRECEDENT (PG-022, okf/concepts/platform-gotchas.md:161-171): 'the memory cost is almost always PHP, not ClickHouse' for continuous-GPS work, and the established fix is to move per-point cost entirely into ClickHouse and return a pre-reduced result (KitRangePathsQuery: O(segments) not O(points), ~1GB refused -> ~20MB proven at 200-kit-org scale). W2 is the same template applied to check-in matching (O(matches) not O(addresses)) -- this is not a novel design, it is the second application of an established pattern.

resource_envelope.growth: Within a single measured 4-hour production window, kits_processed grew 29-32 -> 43 and orgs_processed grew 11 -> 12 (evidence-38240-incident.md). Any duration/memory budget in this PR should assume continued growth past today's snapshot, not size to it.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Current (pre-fix, the incident): O(addresses_per_org) held as a PHP array across the 43-kit loop, copied whole by array_chunk() once per kit, plus $matches[] accumulating with no streaming -- multiplied by UNBOUNDED concurrency (measured peak 17, driven by withoutOverlapping(10)'s expiry-not-duration-cap semantics against 63-209 min cycles) -- measured at ~1.5-3 GB/process, ~29 GB marginal against ~30 GB total headroom (the outage). W2 (this PR): PHP never materializes an address list at all -- ClickHouse computes the match and returns only ~40 rows/cycle at current volume, so per-process PHP footprint becomes O(matches), several orders of magnitude smaller than O(addresses). W3 then caps concurrency independent of cycle duration, bounding the multiplier even in a pathological slow-cycle scenario, so total host footprint stays bounded regardless of how long an individual cycle takes.
unresolved: sc_positions per-kit largest-group row count (GPS fixes in a 15-min lookback for the busiest kit) is not measurable via the zod-CDC-only prod-cardinality probe (sc_positions is ClickHouse-native, not a Postgres CDC mirror) and is not otherwise available read-only in this pipeline; needed to settle design risk 2 (GPS density vs the scan-tuned rollup) before committing to a bbox/CTE shape.

AC2 (duration measured at prod cardinality) and AC5 (EXPLAIN/query_log proof) both require read-only access to production ClickHouse Cloud that this pipeline does not have; can be designed toward but not verified pre-merge.
Design risk 1 (IN vs equality on lower(kit_mapping)) needs an EXPLAIN against Cloud to settle, which is not available here.

reasons: Two MATERIAL design risks are explicitly ticket-flagged as unresolved (IN-vs-equality prune shape; GPS density vs the scan-tuned rollup) and cannot be settled from code reading alone -- both need a Cloud EXPLAIN this pipeline cannot run.

W3's concurrency-ceiling mechanism is a genuinely open design choice (new in-process semaphore vs resurrecting a reverted per-org job dispatcher) with no existing Cache::lock precedent anywhere in the app to default to.

AC2 and AC5 cannot be measured/proven pre-merge given this pipeline's lack of production/Cloud-scale access -- real risk of shipping a design that LOOKS right but is unverified at the exact scale that caused the original outage.
